methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series D → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.5x) to $262M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 5 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.0B - $2.3B.

private.name: Exotec
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series D), post-money $2B

data.narrative:
Outrider, a Series D robotics and manufacturing company founded by Andrew Smith, has raised $262M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable set of eight private and one public company operating in the same sector and stage cohort, including peers such as Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Divergent ($2.3B, Series E), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series C), Agile Robots ($1.0B, Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B, Series C).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression modeling, using the $262M raised as a proxy and applying a typical 1.5x step-up multiplier for Series D advancement, implies a valuation of $393M. Peer-median analysis across the five identified comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.3B. This peer set reflects same-sector positioning and same or adjacent funding stage.

The triangulated analysis implies a valuation range of $334M to $1.8B, with a median of $996M. The substantial spread between the stage-progression method ($393M) and peer-median method ($1.6B) reflects meaningful uncertainty regarding Outrider's positioning relative to contemporaries. Key variables affecting the final valuation include revenue trajectory, customer concentration, path to profitability, and competitive differentiation relative to the identified peer set.
